html:
Oθaakiiwaki‧hina‧ki is the Sauk name for their people. The map places them around Saginaw Bay in Michigan, whose name comes from them: "the place of the Sauk". They are an Algonquian people, farmers of maize and hunters of the woodlands.

In the 1600s, pushed by the Beaver Wars, they moved west to the Green Bay area of Wisconsin, where French traders met them, and later to the Rock River in Illinois. There they grew close to the Meskwaki, or Fox. A disputed treaty of 1804 gave away their Illinois lands; in 1832 Black Hawk led a band back across the Mississippi, and the Black Hawk War followed. The Sauk were then moved to Iowa, Kansas and finally Oklahoma. See Sauk and Meskwaki and Sac and Fox (Oklahoma).
